newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sets the rules for foreign warships.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sets the rules for foreign warships.

text.p: Vietnam said on Thursday it had introduced new rules requiring visiting foreign warships and their crews to respect its sovereignty, independence and national laws.
An announcement in the official Communist Party mouthpiece, the Nhan Dan daily, said the new regulations required foreign navies to arrange visits through diplomatic channels.
Their vessels would be required to follow instructions from Vietnamese port authorities, and captains would be held responsible for the activities of crew members.
It did not elaborate, and the reasons behind the new rules were not explained.
Foreign diplomats in Hanoi said the regulation appeared to refer to a procedural dispute between Vietnam and foreign navies over the hoisting of national flags by visiting vessels.
Hanoi has required foreign warships to hoist its national flag -- a yellow star on a red background -- in place of their own during visits.
The new rules are effective immediately.
